title: Police investigated in death of homeless man
article: The Special Investigations Unit, which investigates deaths or serious injuries involving police, has been piecing together the whereabouts of Stuart Mitchell in the seven hours after police detained him on Jan. 30.
They're investigating whether chest injuries sustained by Mitchell may have stemmed from a run-in with police.
A friend of Mitchell's told the Toronto Star that two cops "jumped" on his chest that night while another female cop told them to "take it easy."
Mitchell, 49, was admitted to a local hospital Jan. 31, complaining of chest pain. Nineteen days later, following a transfer to another hospital, he died.
The SIU is not releasing autopsy results.
Investigators have learned that Mitchell was briefly detained by officers who responded to a gun call at a downtown rooming house about 11:30 p.m.
No gun was found on Mitchell, who was released about 30 minutes later.

On Wednesday, the Special Investigations Unit confirmed Mitchell was involved with police Jan. 30. The agency asked for the public's help to determine what happened to Mitchell from the time police released him at midnight to his arrival at a hostel the next morning.
Mitchell told several people "he had been assaulted by Toronto police officers on the night of January 30, 2000," the SIU said.
Mitchell's older brother, Bob, said Mitchell was a father of three who had worked hard until a few years ago when he suffered from an industrial accident and the death of their brother in 1993.
"I often thought he wouldn't last long in life," said his brother, 53, who works in the music industry.
